source_quote: Exenatide and PB-105 had elimination phase half-life values of 4.8 ± 0.7 and 4.9 ± 1.0 h respectively.
source_location: Results, 'Pharmacokinetics of exenatide and PB-105 (ExC39) in rats' (Figure 5)
route_quote: Two groups of cannulated rats received i.v. injections of exenatide or PB-105 (ExC39) at a dose of 5 µg·mL−1·kg−1.
notes: CITED_NOT_MEASURED: label range 1.5-4 h is only the Introduction citation ('exhibits a short plasma half-life of 1.5–4 h', Parkes 2001; Kolterman 2005, clinical). Measured rat iv exenatide value is 4.8 h.

source_quote: Unmodified PB-105 was rapidly removed from the circulation first in an exponential fashion in the distribution phase followed by a slow-decay elimination phase, with an elimination phase t1/2 of 2.9 ± 0.1 h
source_location: Results, 'Pharmacokinetics of PB-105 (ExC39) and its PEGylated analogues in normal rats' (Figure 10)
route_quote: Five groups of normal Sprague-Dawley rats (n = 3 in each group) each received bolus i.v. injections of PB-105 (ExC39) or its PEGylated analogues at a dose of 5 µg·mL−1·kg−1.
notes: Same paper also reports PB-105 4.9 ± 1.0 h in the separate Fig. 5 exenatide-comparison experiment; label matches the Fig. 10 experiment only.
